Community Manager

Catch Ups with Candice, a resident FAQ, and a search for a dedicated bus driver

Welcome to the September newsletter. Coming into spring, September is shaping up to be another busy month around the village.

This month I'm kicking off Catch Ups with Candice, held fortnightly on Tuesdays. These are an informal opportunity to have a cuppa, ask questions, raise anything on your mind, or simply have a chat.

We are continuing to work on several areas raised through resident feedback, including village communication, activities, and outings. Recruitment for a dedicated bus driver is underway, which we hope will give us more opportunity to get the bus out and about.

We also farewell Rohin and Shane at the end of August and thank them both for their contribution to the village.

There continues to be plenty happening behind the scenes and I'll keep you updated as these progress.

As always, please stop and say hello when you see me around the village — I'm always happy to have a chat.

Check out the below FAQ's for this month.

Warm regards, Candice.
candice.oliver@aveo.com.au

QuestionBest person to contact
My light isn't workingReception. They will put a job in for the maintenance team
I have a complaintResidents can fill out feedback or come speak with the Community Manager directly
I want to hire the MRC or private dining roomReception
The gardens need attentionReception. They will ask for more details and put a job in for the gardening team to complete
I think something is unsafeAny staff member immediately
I need information about my contract or feesAssistant Community Manager or Community Manager
Who do I speak to if I need more help in my homeOur in-home supports team Helen or Nadine — reception can assist
I have a suggestion for the villageFeedback form, speak with the resident committee or speak directly with the Community Manager
How can I make an appointment to see the registered nurseReception emails Shelley and she can then call and make a time, or reception can give Shelley's Aveo email for residents to email directly
What number do I phone the kitchen on3264 0954
Maintenance & Gardening Requests — If you have any maintenance or gardening jobs, please let the office know so a job can be logged. All jobs are to be requested this way. All jobs incurring a charge will be on-charged to your levies.

Quick Contacts

Office — 3862 9020 (Mon–Fri, 8am–4pm)

Catch Ups with Candice

Come along for a cuppa and a chat — every second Tuesday, 10am–12pm, in the Manor. It's a chance to get to know each other, have a chat about what's happening around the village, share your ideas or feedback, or simply pop in and say hello.

Village News

Internet Café

The Internet Café is now fully operational, available for use at any time.

There are 3 nooks in the Manor Private Dining Room and 2 nooks in the MRC Meeting Room. Printing is available at both locations. An easy-to-follow guide is attached to each nook.

'How to use' sessions will be run on Tuesdays from 10:30am in the Manor and on Wednesdays from 2:30pm in the MRC.

Gary's Gardening

Spring is just around the corner, and I am currently spraying the Bindiis and Clover in the lawns and working my way around the village getting the garden beds ready for spring.

A friendly reminder that if you cut, prune, weed, or have any garden waste for collection, please leave it out near the roadway in front of your unit, preferably in a box or tub.

Thank you for helping us keep our village looking neat and tidy as we get ready for Spring!

Welcome in Spring — Creative Competition

What does Spring mean to you? Write a poem, paint, draw, sketch, or photograph something around the village that speaks "Spring" to you! Let your creativity bloom and show us what Spring looks like through your eyes.

Please double-check these dates with the office — the flyer we received lists entries closing Friday 28 August, with the winner announced Monday 31 August, both of which have already passed by the time of this September edition. This may need a corrected flyer for residents.

Aveo Social Media Competition

Share to social media why you love living at Aveo and the winning story will win a $5000 adventure for their community. Record a short video (under 60 seconds) or share photos with a caption about what you love about living at your village, post it to Facebook or Instagram tagging @Aveo / @Aveoretirementliving with #LivingatAveo, and send your completed consent form to mediaenquiries@aveo.com.au.

Please double-check these dates with the office — the flyer we received lists entries closing Friday 21 August and winners notified Friday 28 August, both already passed by this September edition. Worth confirming whether this competition has since closed or been extended before republishing.

Dining

A Little Housekeeping from the Kitchen Team

Just a few friendly reminders from the kitchen team regarding our upcoming events and Bistro Nights.

Event Bookings

For all kitchen events, please remember that bookings are essential and generally close 24 hours prior to the event, or as stated on the event flyer.

All bookings for kitchen events can be found in the blue folder outside the Cinema Room.

We also require accurate numbers for each event to ensure we can prepare the correct amount of food and have enough for everyone attending.

If you are already booked into an event but need to cancel, please provide the kitchen with at least 24 hours' notice. This helps with our planning and, importantly, helps minimise food waste.

September Kitchen Events

  • Roast Nights — Wednesday, 2 September 2026; Wednesday, 16 September 2026
  • Birthday Lunch — Thursday, 24 September 2026
  • Happy Hour — Friday, 25 September 2026
  • Bistro Nights — Friday, 4 September 2026 (Fish Fryday Night); Friday, 11 September 2026 (Full Menu); Friday, 18 September 2026 (Full Menu)
New Bistro Night Start Time — Moving forward, Bistro Nights will start at 5:30pm instead of 6:00pm.

A Little Crockery Reminder

If by chance your crockery finds its way to the kitchen by mistake, it will be placed with the events folder for you to collect.

Finally, if you could kindly check your cupboards for any crockery that may belong to the kitchen, we would really appreciate it. We are currently missing a few items, so any help in returning them would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you for your cooperation and for helping the kitchen team plan, prepare and deliver our events. We really appreciate your support!

— The Kitchen Team

Roast Nights

Meals available 5:00pm till 6:30pm, Nightingale Manor. 2 courses $20.50, 3 courses $22.50.

Bistro Nights

Fridays at the Curlew Restaurant & Cafe. Please note the new start time above: Bistro Nights now begin at 5:30pm. Bookings are required and close Thursday.

Birthday Lunch

Happy Hour with Ren on the Piano

At Happy Hour this month in the Manor we have a special guest. Adrienne comes from a musical family and plays piano and a lot of old-time dance tunes and music (which I'm sure you will all be familiar with).

Adrienne also sings in a Brisbane Choir called Soul Song. This year the choir is participating in a world-wide project called "Be Kind". It is remembering the victims of the 9/11 attack in New York, which happened 25 years ago this year.

Each group member of this choir is encouraged to perform '3 x Random Acts of Kindness' to bring some joy to people. Adrienne would like this event / piano playing at our Happy Hour in the Manor to be one of her Acts of Kindness.

Friday 25th September, from 3:30pm, in the Manor. Pre-drinks 3:30pm, food available from 5:00pm. $17.50 per person — bookings essential, closing 21/09/2026.

Health & Wellbeing

Eye Health Talk

Monday, September 7th, 2:00pm, in the Manor. A free community talk for residents, presented by Ismael Sorefan, Owner Optometrist at Stylish Optometrist. All welcome, just come along — no RSVP needed.

Social Club

Social Club News

The Month That Was

August was a very active month socially in the Village. Almost 90 residents attended the Sausage Sizzle on Exhibition Wednesday in Fountain Court. In addition to the Strawberry Sundae Ice Creams, residents were surprised to be treated to show bags and fairy floss as well! The trial of weekly Happy Hours has seen up to 40 people gathering on Friday afternoons in the MRC. With Rob Rosenlund entertaining during the Happy Hour on 21 August, the numbers swelled to about 60 residents who had a very enjoyable evening.

September Events

A variety of events is planned for September. Look out for the specific flyers with all the details on notice boards, Facebook or on the Residents' Hub (click on 'What's On', then 'Events').

Register your attendance on the lists in The Manor, MRC or on the Residents' Hub:

  • Wednesday 2 September: Fashion Parade and Morning Tea. Cost $10 (register by 28 August). Seating from 9.30am for 10am start. Location is now MRC, not Manor.
  • Monday 14 September: Spring Garden Party (afternoon tea in Fountain Court). No gardening required so wear your "glad rags"! Entry $10 (pay on the day). Register attendance by 11 September. Seating from 2.00pm.
The following events are proposed to be held in the Melody Ridge Centre. Should the situation change, due to the refurbishment, those registered for events will be notified. Also monitor noticeboards, Facebook, Residents' Hub or the screen in The Manor for updates.
  • Sunday 20 September: Musical afternoon featuring one of the most memorable musicals of all time: the 1956 Academy Award winning movie The King and I starring Yul Brynner and Deborah Kerr. Register attendance by 18 September to assist with seating arrangements. Cost $3 payable on entry. Commences at 1.30pm.
  • Thursday 24 September: Sip and Paint. Cost $20 (includes drinks and nibbles, paints and your choice from a variety of different ceramic planters to paint). No artistic talent required! Pay on the day but register attendance by 21 September. Commences at 1.00pm (replaces 3Cs).
  • Saturday 26 September: AFL Grand Final on Big Screen. Free to attend, Bar will be open with some "Footy Food" supplied. Register your attendance by 25 September to assist with seating arrangements.

Future Date Claimers

  • Saturday 3 October, from 5.30pm: Dance Party with the entertainer Fortunato Isgro
  • Saturday 21 November: Craft Fair
  • Wednesday 2 December: Christmas lunch with Fortunato Isgro

Decorate Your Door: Every resident has a front door so start thinking about how you can decorate it for this Christmas competition! Extra points for creativity. Further details in coming newsletters.

Kathy Kingsford
Convenor, Social Club Committee

Tuesday 22nd September in the Manor at 1.15pm. RSVP at Reception. Requests and song ideas are welcome.

Safety

Testing Your Tunstall

Test your pendant and base unit monthly. If you are unsure how to carry out these tests, please speak to the office.

Reminder: have an overnight bag packed in case of an emergency. Keep a list of your current medications with it.

Sales

From the Sales Team

September is here, and with it, the first signs of spring! For those of us who cherish the warmer days, the arrival of this season brings a refreshing change and a perfect opportunity to enjoy the outdoors.

The market has slowed down a little which means people who are looking at coming into a Retirement Village may take a little longer to sell their home.

A lot of people took advantage of the residential market by selling in good times, coming into a Retirement Village and having a bit leftover to enjoy. Real Estate over the years is always up and down so it couldn't stay up forever.

I presently don't have any units to sell but a couple coming soon.

Warm regards, Debbie and Maree

Community Life

Get 2 Know

Who are we? What have we seen? Where have we been? What interests do we have? A wonderful opportunity to hear our guest speakers share stories, memories, and reflections on life, both past and present.

Friday 18th September, 1pm in the Manor. RSVP with reception for seating. If you'd like to be a guest speaker at the next meet-up, let the office know.

Poetry Group

The Poetry Group meeting is cancelled for September and will resume in October. The title for the poem for the next meeting is "He" and can be any type of poem the writer wishes to use.

The theme for September was Haiku.

Bare rooted orchids
living in the coolest fresh air
a gale is no match.
— Deidre P.

No time for anyone
Rush, haste, speed, busyness
No time for anything.

Magnolia comes
Beauty, perfume fills the air
Magnolia falls.
— Judy B.

French Bulldog
Black and other colours
Proud, stubborn and very cute.
Friend to one and all.
— Lorraine Mc

Message from Gary Rowney

I would just like to say a heartfelt thank you for all the love, kindness and respect you have shown me, especially over the past few weeks.

I have very much appreciated your support, and it has truly meant a great deal to me. The kindness you have shown has been outstanding, and I am incredibly grateful to each and every one of you.

Thank you from the bottom of my heart.
